issues.quote: from each of the last [twelve] [month starts]... Build an [80] percent range for [the number I need: one day, or the total over the horizon] from backtest errors of that same kind, using the earlier backtests, and report how often it held on the later ones.
issues.explanation: Splitting 12 monthly backtests into 6 earlier and 6 later rehearsals works for daily errors because each half has 6 x 28 = 168 daily observations. For a 28-day total, each backtest produces only one error, leaving just 6 numbers to cut 10th and 90th percentiles and 6 numbers to test coverage. Even the full [min, max] of 6 continuous i.i.d. errors has an expected out-of-sample coverage of only 5/7 (71.4%), below the promised 80%, and observed coverage on 6 test totals moves in 16.7-point steps. Building and validating an empirical quantile range for a horizon total requires many more backtest dates than 12 monthly starts.
issues.evidence: forecast.backtest.how (12 forecasts of 28 days each); forecast.interval.how (10th and 90th percentiles on first 6 backtests, checked on last 6, which gives 168 daily errors per half but would give n=6 totals per half; compare forecast.interval.by_week_ahead where even n=42 days per half gives noisy 66.7% to 90.5% coverage).
issues.fix: Add a caveat in seg5 and ask_assistant that because each rehearsal yields only one horizon-total error, building and checking a quantile band for a 28-day total requires many more backtest origins (for example, weekly forecast starts over history rather than 12 monthly ones).

issues.quote: hold out a random fifth of the days / 5-fold cross-validation, shuffled, on 851 days
issues.explanation: FACTS reports mape_shuffled_folds = 0.0318 (3.2%) for gradient boosting on calendar features and n_days = 851 for the series, but does not state how many folds were used in forecast.shuffled_folds_vs_backtest or whether all 851 days were included in those folds.
issues.evidence: forecast.shuffled_folds_vs_backtest (describes 'randomly held-out days' with mape_shuffled_folds = 0.0318, with no fold count recorded).
issues.fix: Refer to 'randomly held-out folds of days' in seg1 and 'shuffled cross-validation' in quiz 6-2-q1 without specifying 5 folds / a fifth.

verdict: All core numbers, series values, and quiz keys match facts.json accurately; the main substantive issue is instructing learners to estimate and validate an 80% quantile band for a 28-day total by splitting just 12 monthly backtests in half (n=6 totals per half), plus an unverified 5-fold detail for the shuffled forecast test.
